hero.title: Middle Frontend Developer Resume Skills: *ship with quality & structure*
hero.lede: Past the fundamentals, a mid-level frontend developer is trusted to ship features that stay working. These are the skills that show you write typed, tested, well-structured code — and can own a feature end to end.

quickAnswer.question: What skills should a mid-level frontend developer put on a resume?
quickAnswer.answer: On top of the fundamentals, a middle frontend developer is expected to write typed, tested, maintainable code. Lead with TypeScript, a solid testing habit, state and data management, and API integration — then show you can own a feature: component architecture, code review, and an eye on performance. Tailor the exact mix to the roles you're targeting.

faq.q: What separates a mid-level frontend resume from a junior one?
faq.a: Autonomy and quality. Junior resumes prove you know the fundamentals; mid-level resumes show you ship features that stay working — typed with TypeScript, covered by tests, structured into reusable components, and integrated with real APIs. Back each with a bullet where you owned the work end to end.

faq.q: What are the most important mid-level frontend developer skills?
faq.a: Beyond HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React, employers look for TypeScript, a real testing discipline (unit and integration), state and data management, API integration, component architecture, and awareness of performance. Code review and collaboration start to matter as much as raw output.

faq.q: How many skills should a mid-level frontend resume list?
faq.a: Around 12–16 curated skills. Enough to cover your core stack plus testing, TypeScript and the specific technologies a role names — but every one should be defensible in an interview. Depth you can discuss beats a long list of tools you've only touched once.

faq.q: Should a mid-level frontend developer list soft skills?
faq.a: Yes, in context. At this stage, code review, collaboration and ownership are real signals — prove them with a bullet like "Reviewed PRs and mentored a junior on component patterns" rather than listing "teamwork" on its own.
